We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. Valve has good news and bad news for anyone interested in buying a Steam Machine. All current reservations for the 512GB model have been fulfilled and there's stock remaining, so if you want one you can just head over to the purchase page and buy it—but the 2TB model is in shorter supply so signups for the waitlist are no longer being taken. And, sorry to say, there's also worse news: Valve says it won't be able to produce them in the quantities it had planned, and the price could increase. Despite their high prices, demand for Steam Machines was high enough that Valve implemented a randomized lottery system to buy one: Prospective purchasers signed up for a shot, a randomized selection were put in a reservation queue with a Steam Machine reserved in their name, and everyone else went to the waiting list to be notified when more reservation spots came open. Valve said in July that it expected to have the reservation queue caught up by the end of 2026, and that's now the case with the 512GB model: They're in an "an add-to-cart status," meaning that while supplies last, you can purchase one and it will be shipped straight away. The situation is less happy for people waiting for the 2TB model, though. In an update posted today, Valve said all reservation holders have been sent their invitations to purchase but there are still people on the waiting list; those people won't lose their positions, but no one else will be allowed to join. In a distressing update on Steam Machine stock and pricing, Valve says "we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them" as the RAM and storage markets remain crunched. "We've been able to fulfill all current reservations for the 512GB model with no waitlist remaining, and have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders," Valve says in a new Steam post. Here comes the other shoe: "However, we are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts." 512GB Steam Machines can be purchased directly "while supplies last," Valve says, but once the current stock runs dry, the company will "flip it to out-of-stock rather than begin building another waitlist." The 2TB model is in worse shape. While Valve has "finished getting purchases invites out to all reservation holders," nobody still on the waitlist is "guaranteed a unit." However, Valve says everyone on the waitlist "will retain their position in line." That waitlist is now being closed, however, as "there are more people on the waitlist than units available." As a result, the 2TB Steam Machine will also show as out-of-stock in the store. "You are welcome to choose to purchase a 512GB model instead (while supplies last)," Valve says. But you will have to leave the 2TB waitlist to do that. Valve expects to have "more information" come January, but I wouldn't bet on good news, as the RAM and storage drought is projected to continue well beyond January amid AI data center fever.
